card.does: Lets power through, and cuts it off while its front bar presses against something.
card.gives: Gives: a stop when your robot bumps into a wall or a box.
card.needs: Needs: a place in the power line (red), at the front of the chassis (frame).
card.popularMechanics: A robot vacuum cleaner feels its way round a room with a bumper switch like this.
card.safetyNote: Real bumper switches are small parts, so build with an adult nearby.

failureModes.cardLine: Across the battery pack: it drains the pack fast until its bar is pressed.
failureModes.hint: This bumper switch closes a loop with nothing in it that uses power
failureModes.teachingNote: A bumper switch stays closed until its bar is pressed. Wired straight across the battery pack, it joins plus to minus the whole time nothing touches it, so it makes a short circuit instead of stopping a part.

failureModes.cardLine: Not in the loop: a bump changes nothing.
failureModes.hint: This bumper switch is not in a loop with the battery pack
failureModes.teachingNote: A bumper switch stops only the loop it sits in. Wired off to one side, with no loop running through it, a bump changes nothing.
